summary: The Secretary for Health, Professor Lo Chung-mau, led a delegation to attend the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 held in Beijing today (October 17) to have in-depth discussions and exchanges with senior health officials from around the world, as well as experts and academics in the traditional medicine field on issues related to traditional medicine, including legislation, policy and regulation, scientific research, talent cultivation, empowerment of artificial intelligence, as well as promotion of integration of traditional medicine into healthcare service systems. The conference is jointly organised by the People's Government of Beijing Municipality, the National Health Commission (NHC), the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in collaboration with the World Health Organization. At the opening ceremony, Professor Lo listened to Premier Li Qiang's keynote speech. title: FS meets with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and senior executives of multinational financial institution in Bangkok (with photos/video)
summary: The Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, continued his visit to Bangkok, Thailand, this morning (October 17). Mr Chan met with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Thailand, Mr Ekniti Nitithanprapas, in the morning to exchange views on further strengthening economic, trade and financial co-operation between Hong Kong and Thailand. The two sides explored ways to deepen co-operation and connect foreign direct investment in Thailand with Hong Kong's capital market to further support enterprises investing and expanding their businesses in Thailand. Mr Chan said that Hong Kong could leverage its strengths as an international financial centre to provide comprehensive investment and financing support for enterprises in Thailand. Hong Kong also welcomed closer regulatory co-operation between the two securities markets to encourage dual listings by enterprises from both places and strengthen capital market ties. title: Hospital Authority Family Medicine Outpatient Services arrangements on public holiday on day following Chung Yeung Festival
summary: The following is issued on behalf of the Hospital Authority: ​The Hospital Authority (HA) spokesperson today (October 17) announced that 15 Family Medicine Clinics (FMCs) will provide public holiday family medicine outpatient services on the public holiday on the day following the Chung Yeung Festival (October 19) (see table below). Members of the public may book an appointment through the telephone appointment system, the eHealth mobile application or the "Book FMC" function in the "HA Go" mobile application. The spokesperson reminded the public to stay vigilant about personal and environmental hygiene during the holiday to avoid spreading diseases. Members of the public who develop respiratory symptoms should wear masks and seek medical advice promptly. The spokesperson emphasised that non-emergency patients should avoid using Accident and Emergency (A&E) services and instead seek treatment at FMCs, private doctors or 24-hour outpatient services at private hospitals to reduce pressure on public hospital A&Es. title: Territory-wide flag day today
summary: Yang Memorial Methodist Social Service has been issued a Public Subscription Permit to hold a territory-wide flag sale from 7am to 12.30pm today (October 17), a spokesman for the Social Welfare Department (SWD) said. Details of the charitable fund-raising activities, including any updated information, covered by the issued Public Subscription Permits have been published on the GovHK website ( www.gov.hk/en/theme/fundraising/search ). Permits for flag days containing information on contact methods of the flag-selling organisations and the approved flag-selling activities have also been uploaded to the SWD's website ( www.swd.gov.hk/en/ngo/controlofc/flagdays ) for reference. For enquiries, please call the SWD's hotline at 2343 2255, or the designated hotline of the 1823 Call Centre at 3142 2678. In the case of suspected fraudulent flag day activities, people should not make any donation and should immediately report the matter to the Police, the spokesman added.

title: CFS finds samples of mung bean starch sheet and its related product not in compliance with requirement on preservative
summary: The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (October 16) that samples of two batches of mung bean starch sheet and its related product were found not in compliance with the requirement of the Preservatives in Food Regulation (Cap. 132BD) (the Regulation). The CFS is following up on the incident. Product details are as follows: Product name: (Not available in English) Weight: 500 grams Manufacture dates: June 27, 2026; July 9, 2026 Place of origin: China Sole distributor: Zhuang Ji Food Trade Company A spokesman for the CFS said, "The CFS collected two samples of mung bean starch sheet and its related product sold and supplied by the above-mentioned sole distributor for testing. The test results showed that the two samples contained sodium dehydroacetate at a level of 69 and 61 parts per million respectively, not in compliance with the requirement of the Regulation. Prosecution will be instituted should there be sufficient evidence." "The CFS has informed the vendor concerned of the matter concerned, and instructed it to stop selling and remove from shelves the affected batches of the product concerned, and to initiate a recall.

title: Demand roars, supply whispers: Monetary policy and housing in Canada
summary: We examine the effects of monetary policy shocks on the Canadian housing market. Using high-frequency surprises around fixed announcement dates as an instrument in a Bayesian VAR, we estimate the responses of house prices, housing starts, building permits, resales, inventories, and mortgage purchases to a contractionary monetary policy shock. An increase in the policy rate leads to a substantial and persistent decline in average house prices. Housing starts and building permits fall, but their implied effects on the future housing stock are both slow and modest. Interpreted through the lens of market equilibrium, these results are most consistent with a stronger response of housing demand than housing supply.

summary: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 16) announced that one new melioidosis case was recorded in the past week (October 9 to 15). The CHP appealed to members of the public to maintain personal and environmental hygiene to prevent melioidosis. The CHP also specifically reminded high-risk groups, including the elderly and people with underlying diseases, to avoid contact with soil or muddy water after typhoons or storms with a view to lowering infection risk. The case involves a 74-year-old female with underlying illnesses who lived in Sham Shui Po District. On October 4, she presented with a fever and cough with sputum. Her clinical diagnosis was pneumonia. Her clinical sample tested positive for Burkholderia pseudomallei. The patient passed away on October 8 and the cause of death is under investigation. A spokesman for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) said that the passenger arrived at Hong Kong International Airport from Brazil via Ethiopia on March 22 this year. The woman was prosecuted by the AFCD for illegal import of specimens of endangered species. Similar special circumstances are also encountered in private market transactions. title: CHP continues to implement multipronged strategy to curb spread of Mpox
summary: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 16) recorded an imported Mpox (also known as Monkeypox) case. There has been a significant increase in Mpox cases in Hong Kong since August 2026. To curb the spread of Mpox, the CHP has adopted a multipronged approach, including conducting comprehensive epidemiological investigation and analysis to break transmission chains, enhancing collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to facilitate vaccination for individuals with high-risk exposure and increase their willingness to receive the Mpox vaccine, and strengthening public awareness and education efforts. The multipronged strategy has yielded initial effects. The number of confirmed cases recorded in the first 15 days of October has dropped significantly by more than 60 per cent compared to the same period last month (September), while the number of vaccination doses administered under the Mpox vaccination programme in the first two weeks of October has increased by more than 60 per cent compared to the same period last month. About 80 orchestras will participate in the Chinese Orchestra Interflow in six classes at the Auditorium of the Tuen Mun Town Hall from November 16 to 19. For the Symphony Orchestra Interflow, about 60 orchestras in four classes will perform at the Concert Hall of the Hong Kong Cultural Centre from November 23 to 25. About 50 orchestras will participate in the String Orchestra Interflow in four classes at the Auditorium of the Yuen Long Theatre from December 8 to 10. About 90 bands will take part in six classes in the Symphonic Band Interflow at the Arena of Queen Elizabeth Stadium from December 1 to 4. title: Labour Department to hold online briefing for employers of foreign domestic helpers
summary: The Labour Department (LD) will hold an online briefing on the employment of foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) on November 19 (Thursday), at 7pm. Enrolment is now open. The online briefing will provide an overview of the employment rights and obligations of employers of FDHs. Representatives from the Immigration Department will also speak on the Immigration Ordinance and legislation related to the employment of FDHs, as well as to share insights on building a safe community. Employers of FDHs, especially first-time employers, are welcome to attend. The online briefing will be conducted in Cantonese via Zoom, and admission is free. Interested parties may register online at the LD's dedicated FDH Portal ( www.fdh.labour.gov.hk ), or download the enrolment form ( www.fdh.labour.gov.hk/res/pdf/Enrolment_Form_ER.pdf ) and submit it by email ( fdh-enquiry@labour.gov.hk ) or by fax (3101 0604). The deadline for enrolment is November 17 (Tuesday). The quota will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. For enquiries, please contact the LD at 3582 8995.

title: Official ceremony to commemorate 160th anniversary of birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen
summary: The Government announced today (October 16) that an official ceremony will be held on November 12 to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen. November 12, 2026, marks the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen, a great national hero, a great patriot and a great forerunner of China's democratic revolution. In commemoration of Dr Sun Yat-sen's immortal contributions to national independence, social progress and the people's well-being, the Government will hold an official ceremony at Sun Yat Sen Memorial Park on the morning of November 12. Hongkong Post will issue special stamps to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen on the same day. Government departments and community organisations will organise a series of commemorative activities starting this month to allow members of the public to gain a better understanding of his life and contributions from diverse perspectives. These activities include exhibitions, seminars, guided tours, film screenings, student and youth exchange tours to the Chinese Mainland, local heritage trail visits, and a parent-child quiz competition. title: 2026 final register for Rural Representative Election published today
summary: The 2026 final register for the Rural Representative Election (RRE) was published today (October 16). The final register contains the particulars of the registered electors of Existing Villages, Indigenous Villages, Composite Indigenous Villages and Market Towns. Registered electors may log into the RRE Voter Registration Information Enquiry System through the RRE website ( www.had.gov.hk/rre ) for perusal of their own registration particulars. They may also call the RRE hotline at 2152 1521 during ordinary business hours for enquiries about the relevant information. A full copy of the final register is placed at the office of the Electoral Registration Officer located at the Home Affairs Department (HAD), 11/F, Southorn Centre, 130 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai. Copies of the specific divisions of the final register for Rural Areas that belong to the Rural Committees concerned are placed at the offices of the Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in the respective New Territories District Offices (NTDOs), the office addresses of which are set out on the RRE website. summary: ​The International Organizations (Privileges and Immunities) (The International Criminal Police Organization-INTERPOL) (231st Executive Committee Session and 94th General Assembly Session) Order was gazetted today (October 16). The Central People's Government and The International Criminal Police Organization-INTERPOL (INTERPOL) signed an agreement on the granting of privileges and immunities to INTERPOL and the persons connected with it for the purposes of the 231st Executive Committee Session and 94th General Assembly (GA) session to be held in Hong Kong. The Order was made by the Chief Executive in Council under the International Organizations (Privileges and Immunities) Ordinance (Cap. 558). The Order seeks to implement the privileges and immunities as provided under the agreement. The GA is the highest governing body of INTERPOL. It meets yearly for representatives of member countries to discuss international policing issues and foster collaboration. The 94th GA will be held in Hong Kong from November 30 to December 3, 2026. title: Offshore forwards and exchange rate transmission in emerging markets
summary: We study how offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) markets transmit exchange-rate pressures to domestic currency markets. Using unique transaction-level data on the universe of centrally cleared NDFs for ten emerging-market currencies over 2013–2025, we show that offshore NDF order flow moves both offshore forward and domestic spot exchange rates and widens the offshore–onshore forward spread.

title: Safety Zone; Cumberland River, Hendersonville, TN
issuer: Homeland Security Department; Coast Guard
summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to establish a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Cumberland River from mile marker 221.7 to 222. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with an overwater fireworks display. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Ohio Valley, or their designated representative.

title: The Welfare Food (Amendment) (England and Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Welfare Food Regulations 1996 (S.I. 1996/1434) (“the 1996 Regulations”). Regulations 3 to 10 amend the 1996 Regulations to replace references to day care with childcare and to update references to childcare legislation in England and Wales which have been updated since the 1996 Regulations came into force. title: Prudential Standard FSI 6-Liquidity Risk Management for Insurers
summary: The Prudential Authority is publishing the proposed Prudential Standard FSI 6 – Liquidity Risk Management for Insurers (Standard) for formal consultation. The first draft of the Standard was released for informal public consultation on 28 May 2024 and the relevant comments received through that process were incorporated into the revised draft Standard. The Standard seeks to strengthen the regulatory framework for identifying, assessing, monitoring, managing and reporting liquidity risk by insurers and is intended to repeal and replace the current Prudential Standard FSI 6 – Liquidity Risk Assessment for Insurers which does not adequately address insurers’ resilience to sudden cash flow pressures and seeks to close this gap by aligning domestic requirements with the International Association of Insurance Supervisors’ framework. title: When less is more: behavioral effects of CBDC holding limits
summary: Holding limits are a central design feature of proposed retail central bank digital currencies (CBDC). While such limits mechanically prevent individuals from exceeding a maximum balance, they may also generate behavioral responses whose directions are a priori unclear. We conducted an incentivized online experiment with participants from four euro-area countries, exogenously varying the presence and level of a holding limit to causally separate direct mechanical effects from behavioral effects. We find that behavioral responses increase holdings of the means of payment subject to the holding limit, consistent with an attraction effect. This effect is material only when the limit is high enough. Enabling reverse waterfall —automatic conversion into this limited means of payment— increases adoption while reducing holdings. These results suggest that combining holding limits with automatic funding mechanisms can support CBDC use while containing holdings, thereby helping to mitigate potential financial stability risks.

title: Stop believing in haircuts - at least the way you think about them
summary: We study how frictions impact haircut setting in repo markets. Using transaction-level supervisory data and exploiting the 2021 introduction of the binding leverage ratio requirement, we show that three frictions jointly shape haircuts in the bilateral dealer-to-client segment: dealer balance sheet constraints, collateral convenience yields, and client outside options. In collateral-driven repos, binding leverage constraints and broader client outside options both raise haircuts, while higher convenience yields push them down. In funding-driven trades, the leverage constraint has no effect, higher convenience yields raise haircuts through the rehypothecation channel, and broader client outside options lower them. We rationalise these patterns in a bilateral bargaining model with periodic haircut renegotiation. Consistent with the model, constrained dealers exhibit higher repo-rate volatility and weaker pass-through of ECB policy rate changes in the collateral-driven segment. Post-crisis bank regulation thus carries potential unintended consequences for repo market functioning and the transmission of monetary policy.

issuer: Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by certification test results of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) on the affected helicopters, which revealed that the installed CCHB could result in fuel leakage following a survivable accident. This proposed AD would require modification of the CCHB and fuel system and installation of structural reinforcement. This proposed AD would also prohibit installing a certain CCHB on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Hong Kong Customs takes territory-wide law enforcement actions against illicit cigarette selling points (with photos)
summary: Hong Kong Customs has been mounting a decoy operation targeting cigarette retail points in various districts in Hong Kong since October 7. A total of about 120 000 suspected illicit cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $540,000 and a duty potential of about $400,000, were seized. Ten persons were arrested. During the operation, Customs officers disguised as customers conducted test buys at different cigarette retail points, including newsstands, stores and grocery shops. Some retail points were found to offer cigarettes for sale at a price less than the statutory duty imposed thereon. As at today (October 14), Customs has taken prompt enforcement actions against ten cigarette retail points in Tuen Mun, Tsing Yi, Tsuen Wan, Kwai Chung, Sham Shui Po, Tsz Wan Shan, Pok Fu Lam and North Point, and arrested shop owners and staff. Ten persons, comprising three men and seven women aged between 26 and 73, were arrested. ​ As part of the new phase of tobacco control measures, the Government gazetted the Tobacco Control Legislation (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 (the Amendment Ordinance) on September 19, 2025.
